Yes to both: MathOp's operator StringLiteralField values list includes 'sqrt' (treated as a unary operator, Math.sqrt). It does NOT support 'atan' — the allowed values are add, subtract, multiply, divide, sine, cosine, tan, min, max, modulo, power, log, sqrt, round, floor, ceil, abs, rad, deg; 'atan' is not among them.

Per AccessorOp's description and its execute() implementation, the available variables are: d (the current data row), i (the row's index), data (the full data array), op() (function to access other operators' outputs/params by path), sequenceTime (current timeline position), frame (current frame number), totalFrames, and sequence (timeline metadata) — plus whatever utilities are exposed via freeExports (e.g. d3, turf, etc.).

MapStyleOp was a pass-through node that only existed to expose a preset map style URL as a string output; it was removed in schema migration 014 ('remove-map-style-op'). The migration's `up` function finds edges from MapStyleOp.out.mapStyle into MaplibreBasemapOp.par.mapStyle, inlines that style URL value directly onto the MaplibreBasemapOp node's mapStyle input, and deletes the MapStyleOp nodes and their edges (falling back to the CARTO_DARK style URL if no value was set). The `down` function reverses this by recreating a MapStyleOp node (only for MaplibreBasemapOp nodes whose mapStyle isn't already fed by an edge) and reconnecting it.

Migration 006 renamed the Theatre.js timeline sheet ID from 'Nodes' to 'Noodles' inside project.timeline.sheetsById (and reverses that rename on downgrade); despite the migration's label, it is a timeline-sheet rename, not a node/operator rename.
DateOp was renamed to DateTimeOp in schema migration 008 (all nodes of type 'DateOp' are changed to type 'DateTimeOp').

Migration 013 ('add-time-markers') adds an empty `markers` array to the timeline's Noodles sheet sequence data (project.timeline.sheetsById.Noodles.sequence.markers), if a sequence exists and markers aren't already present.

An edge's id must be the string `${source}.${sourceHandle}->${target}.${targetHandle}` — i.e. the source node id, a dot, the source handle (e.g. 'out.result'), '->', the target node id, a dot, and the target handle (e.g. 'par.data'). This is implemented by the `edgeId()` helper in noodles-editor/src/noodles/utils/migration-utils.ts.
'par.' (e.g. targetHandle: 'par.data').
'out.' (e.g. sourceHandle: 'out.result').

14 — NOODLES_VERSION is computed as the max version number among files in src/noodles/__migrations__ (currently up to 014-remove-map-style-op.ts), and all example projects in noodles-editor/src/examples/*/noodles.json have "version": 14. (Note: AGENTS.md itself says 'Version 6 is current', which is out of date relative to the actual repository state.)

The '@/' prefix is the `projectScheme` constant (defined in noodles-editor/src/noodles/utils/filesystem.ts as '@/'); it marks the path as relative to the current project's own data/asset directory rather than an absolute path or remote URL, so FileOp strips this prefix and reads the file from the project's local storage.
Node ids are Unix-style fully-qualified paths starting with '/', e.g. '/data-loader', '/arc-layer', or nested paths like '/container/child' for operators inside a container.
op('/data-loader').out.data

op('./sibling') resolves to an operator named 'sibling' in the same container (parent directory) as the current/context operator — i.e. it's relative to the context operator's own container, analogous to a Unix relative path.
A nested operator is addressed by joining the container's path with the child's name using '/', e.g. an operator named 'filter' inside a container '/analysis' is addressed as '/analysis/filter'.

Exactly one — each input (target handle) accepts a single connection; per the onConnect logic in noodles-editor/src/noodles/hooks/use-project-modifications.ts, connecting a new edge to a target handle that already has an edge replaces the existing edge rather than adding a second one, unless the target field is a ListField (which allows multiple incoming connections).
